failures.gap: The construction or argument owed under proved=annex:p15.stieltjes-construction is not written out in full. The endpoint-limit step proves only the lower end, that inf F is the limit at minus infinity. The upper end is dismissed with 'The upper-end proof is the reversed argument' (handbook/annex/p15/measure-extension.tex line 296), which is a 'similarly' in place of written steps. That upper-end fact, F(infinity) = sup F as the limit at plus infinity including the infinite case, is needed later for targets with right endpoint infinity (annex lines 383-385). Second, the stated conclusion 'Its values on bounded intervals are finite' (body handbook/parts/p15/measure-extension.tex lines 211-212) is never proved for bounded intervals other than the finite-endpoint members I(a,b). The monotonicity step from containment in some (-n,n] is not written (annex lines 401-411).

The construction or argument owed under proved=annex:p15.cdf-existence depends on an unstated assumption. The theorem concludes that the law of Q_F equals mu_F and that it is the unique Borel probability law with cumulative function F (body lines 297-299). For this the proof (handbook/annex/p15/measure-extension.tex lines 512-516) cites thm:p15-cdf-laws. That theorem's statement covers only two real random variables (handbook/parts/p15/measurable-probability.tex lines 443-444), and the handbook defines a CDF only for a real random variable (lines 417-425). mu_F, and any Borel probability measure with the same ray values, is never shown to be the law of a real random variable, for example the identity map on (R, B(R), mu_F). No direct argument on the ray pi-system or via the Stieltjes uniqueness clause is written either. So the equality-of-laws and uniqueness conclusions lack a written step.

The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.absolute-iterated-series is not supplied. The series half of the proof connects the corollary's sums to Fubini's integrals only through two bare assertions. The first is 'The assumed sum is the first iterated absolute integral, because integration with respect to kappa is summation' (handbook/annex/p15/product-measures.tex 514-515). The second is 'counting-measure integration of that integrable section equals the sum' (519-521). Neither identity is derived in this proof or established anywhere on the route: the integral against counting measure on N+ of a nonnegative g equals the sum of g(n), and the signed version holds for an absolutely summable section. The closest result, thm:p15-expectation-law-integral (handbook/parts/p15/integration-expectation.tex 324-348), gives the sum formula only for countable atomic probability spaces. Three identifications are therefore unwritten: the hypothesis sum of the integrals of |f_n| with Fubini's premise, H with the section absolute integral (516-518), and S with Fubini's second section-integral function (522-523). All other parts of C013 (the Tonelli criterion at 499-504, product measurability of F, the absolute-convergence bound, integrability of each f_n) are written.

The 'construction or argument' and the 'full treatment promised by its declared status' (proved=annex:p15.stieltjes-construction) are not fully supplied. In handbook/annex/p15/measure-extension.tex, the endpoint-limit step (lines 288-296) writes only the lower end (inf F is the limit at minus infinity). It disposes of the upper end with 'The upper-end proof is the reversed argument' (line 296), which is a 'similarly'-type elision. The unwritten upper-end fact is that F(n) increases to F(inf)=sup F, including when sup F is infinite. The proof uses it at lines 383-385 and 387-391 to truncate targets with b = infinity. So the following all depend on a step that is not written: the countable covering bound for unbounded targets (395-399), the second partition condition, the premeasure, existence of mu_F with mu_F(I(a,inf))=F(inf)-F(a), and mu_F(R)=F(inf)-F(-inf) (401-407). C008 becomes covered once the upper-end case is written out.

The construction or argument is not written in full. In annex:p15.conditional-existence (handbook/annex/p15/conditional-expectation.tex lines 23-31) P is restricted to G and the proved Radon-Nikodym theorem is applied on (Omega,G,P|_G). That gives nu_pm(A) = int_A Z_pm d(P|_G). Lines 32-39 then say Z_pm are integrable with integrals EX^pm and write int_A Z dP = nu_+(A) - nu_-(A). This quietly swaps P|_G-integrals of G-measurable functions for P-integrals. No step or citation supports that swap, and no handbook result states it. It would follow from thm:p15-expectation-law-integral applied to the identity map (Omega,F0)->(Omega,G), or from G-simple approximation (thm:p15-measurable-limits) plus monotone convergence on both spaces. As written, the argument that the constructed Z satisfies the P-integral identity and P-integrability required by def:p15-general-conditional-expectation has an unwritten step. Every other element is present: integrability and E|Z|<=E|X| (annex 5-14), a.e. uniqueness (15-21), the source's X+/X- construction (23-39; Durrett p. 207, PDF 215), no completion (41), and the worked a.e.-uniqueness boundary (body 365-371, annex 727-739).

The success condition requires 'construction or argument ... and the full treatment promised by its declared status' (proved=annex:p15.feller-largest-term-inequality). This is not met for the non-strict case. The promised comparison P(|S|>=t) >= 1/2 P(max_i|Y_i|>=t) carries the stated q_>= bound and the 'exact source CDF form' V.(5.10), which is the preserved source variant with a non-strict left side. The annex discharges it only with 'The same reasoning with M>=t gives the non-strict comparison' (handbook/annex/p15/feller-weak-law-presentation.tex 147-149). That is a 'similarly' step, not written steps. The strict case, the four-pair invariance and the exponential/CDF reductions are fully written.

The success condition requires 'construction or argument ... and the full treatment promised by its declared status' (proved=annex:p15.levy-symmetric-maximal). This is not met for the promised non-strict case. The body says the first inequality 'also holds with both strict inequalities replaced by non-strict ones' (handbook/parts/p15/weak-laws-and-triangular-arrays.tex 246-247). The annex gives only a sketch: 'use the first crossing of |T_k|>=t, split at T_k>=t and T_k<=-t, and use the same argument with terminal threshold >=t' (handbook/annex/p15/weak-laws-and-triangular-arrays.tex 379-381). That is a 'same argument' step, not written steps. Both strict inequalities are fully proved.

The hypotheses are not plainly stated. Body line 345 reads 'positive black weight b, red weight r and same-color reinforcement c>0'. That wording puts a positivity condition on b and c but none on the red weight r. The conclusion that the c_n are 'precisely the moments of beta(b/c,r/c)', which Hausdorff uniqueness then uses to identify the mixing law, needs r>0. The handbook defines beta(alpha,beta) only for alpha,beta>0 (def:p15-beta-integral), and the cited exchangeability theorem thm:p15-polya-word-law assumes r>0. At r=0 the formula gives c_n=1, which are the moments of delta_1, and no beta law exists. So r>0 is an unstated assumption on the plain reading. Every other element is present: the product and gamma forms of c_n, the empty-product convention, the beta moments, the Hausdorff identification, the word and count probabilities, and agreement with the direct urn law (body 344-358, annex 555-584, held Feller II PDF pp. 244-245 = printed 229-230).

The worked boundary is missing for this entry. def:p15-regular-conditional-law (handbook/parts/p15/regular-conditional-laws.tex lines 49-51) says the regular-conditional-probability special case (S=Omega, target sigma-algebra F_0, X the identity) 'needs an existence hypothesis on the outcome space itself'. That is, it claims a regular conditional law need not exist unless (Omega,F_0) satisfies some hypothesis. Nothing on the handbook route shows this. No probability space and sub-sigma-algebra G are given for which no probability kernel from (Omega,G) to (Omega,F_0) satisfies the defining identities, and no argument for the necessity is written. The only support is the citation at conditioning-independence-and-information-w02b-p15-008.tex lines 235-239. It points to Durrett p. 214 (PDF p. 222), which says such laws do not always exist and credits Dieudonne (1948) without giving the example. That is a citation where a demonstration is owed. The countable-cocountable model (w02b-p15-008 annex lines 171-269) does not fill the gap: it shows a source-sense law that cannot be repaired, but a regular conditional law still exists in that model. Owed: a written model in which no regular conditional probability exists, with its proof, or a written argument that establishes the stated need for a hypothesis.

The success condition asks for the full proof that proved=annex:p15.convolution-law promises, for every asserted identity. The second cumulative form, (F*G)(z) = int G(z-x) dF(x) (body handbook/parts/p15/convolution-gamma-normal.tex l.115), rests only on annex l.117: 'The other order similarly gives G(z-x)'. The fixed-x inner evaluation, int 1{x+y<=z} dnu(y) = nu((-inf,z-x]) = G(z-x), is never written. Under the audit rule, 'similarly' in place of written steps counts as partial. Every other assertion of the entry is proved at annex l.100-150. The omitted step is an exact relabelling of the displayed fixed-y computation at annex l.112-115, so one displayed line would close the gap.

The success condition asks for the full proof that proved=annex:p15.beta-gamma-convolution promises. The source rescaling identity, int_0^z (z-y)^(alpha-1) y^(beta-1) dy = z^(alpha+beta-1) B(beta,alpha) (body l.256-260), is a step both gamma-sum routes depend on. Annex l.307 supplies it only as 'The change y=zu, z>0, similarly gives the exact source rescaling identity' before displaying the outcome. Two steps are not written: the measure-scaling factor z of the substitution (thm:p15-affine-lebesgue with c=z; the held Durrett p.51 writes 'dy = x du'), and the bookkeeping z * z^(alpha-1) * z^(beta-1) = z^(alpha+beta-1). The parallel substitution v=1-u one sentence earlier does state its scaling factor. Under the audit rule, 'similarly' in place of written steps counts as partial. Every other assertion is argued at annex l.296-400, including both source routes to B = Gamma*Gamma/Gamma.
